object_types.name: Student
object_types.definition: A person pursuing education at the university, identified by a unique student number.

source_references.excerpt: Students have a student number.

object_types.name: Offering
object_types.definition: A specific instance of a course offered in a particular semester, identified by an offering ID.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly. A course offering is a specific course offered in a specific semester.

object_types.name: MaxCapacity

ambiguities.description: Student enrollment optionality: The transcript states that 'Students enroll in course offerings' but does not explicitly state whether every student must be enrolled in at least one offering, or whether every offering must have at least one enrolled student. Is enrollment mandatory from the student's perspective, or can a student exist without any enrollments? Is it mandatory from the offering's perspective, or can an offering be created without any enrolled students?

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: Grade assignment conditions: The transcript states 'At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.' This implies grades are assigned only for offerings in which the student is enrolled, but it is unclear whether every enrollment must result in a grade, or if there are cases (e.g., withdrawal, incomplete) where a student might be enrolled but not receive a grade.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. The grade is one of A, B, C, D, or F. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Instructor multi-offering capability: The transcript states 'An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester' but does not specify an upper limit or whether an instructor must teach at least one offering. What is the minimum and maximum number of offerings an instructor can teach, and are there any constraints on the total number across different semesters?

source_references.excerpt: An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Course offering multiplicity: The transcript states 'The same course can have multiple offerings' and 'Each offering is of exactly one course' but does not explicitly state whether a course must have at least one offering. Can a course exist without any offerings, or is at least one offering mandatory?

source_references.excerpt: So the same course can have multiple offerings? Right. Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester.

ambiguities.description: Credit value constraint precision: The transcript states credit values are 'usually between 1 and 6' but uses the word 'usually' which suggests this may not be a hard constraint. Does the system enforce this range strictly, or are other values possible in exceptional cases?

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.
